answer: Sybil resistance can come from demanding storage proofs that grow with operator size: the k-th key linked to one operator by a shared bridge or timing ripple must keep a unique replica of 10*k GB online. The 1st key stores 10 GB, the 1,000th stores 10 TB, so the whole farm of 1,000 holds about 5 PB, while a lone honest agent stores almost nothing. A glacier of idle disks makes each extra fake costlier than the last. Weakness: cloud rentals can hide who owns the keys.
